Chapter 5: Holding On and Letting Go—The Struggle to Trust Again.
Trust. It’s such a delicate thing, isn’t it? Especially if you’re someone who’s been let down over and over again. Imagine being a child in foster care, having to decide—sometimes every single day—whether it’s worth it to open up to someone new. Each connection feels like a bit of a gamble. You hope things will be different this time… but that fear of getting hurt again? It never really goes away. It just sits there, quietly waiting.
Early on, this boy learns a tough lesson: promises don’t always mean much. Grown-ups say they’ll be back, or that life will get better, but too often, those words just float away. The sting of disappointment lingers long after, leaving behind scars that take ages to heal. So, what happens? It starts to feel safer to keep your distance—to trust only yourself, and maybe the quiet presence of Doggie. Most folks don’t realize just how quickly a child can learn to hide those real, aching feelings. It’s almost like slipping on a brave mask, even when everything hurts on the inside.
But sometimes—just sometimes—the walls come down. Maybe it’s a foster parent who really cares, a teacher who actually listens, or a friend who just gets it, without asking for explanations. Those moments? They’re precious. But they’re also fragile. One misunderstanding, one sudden change, and everything can fall apart. So, the boy learns to treasure these connections while they last, always ready for the day they might slip away.
Here’s something a lot of people miss: the struggle to trust isn’t only about other people. It’s about learning to believe in yourself, too. You can probably picture the boy, wrestling with guilt and this nagging sense that maybe all the chaos is his fault. It takes a lot of time—and some truly caring adults—for those feelings to start shifting. Healing isn’t a straight line, and yeah, there are plenty of setbacks along the way. But every good experience, no matter how small, helps that sense of confidence grow bit by bit.
Of course, there are bumps in the road. Maybe a foster placement ends suddenly, or a friend moves away, or yet another promise is broken. Each loss is a sharp reminder of how unpredictable life can be. But slowly, the boy starts to realize that he can survive these disappointments. New sources of strength appear, sometimes in the most unexpected places. The scars don’t vanish, but something remarkable happens—resilience begins to take root.
In the quiet moments, maybe late at night, the boy wonders what it really means to trust again. It’s not about erasing the past, or pretending everything’s perfect. It’s about finding just enough courage to hope—to believe that something good could still happen, even if you don’t see any proof yet. Healing, he comes to understand, isn’t a destination. It’s a journey, and every little step forward counts as a win.
So, when you think about survival, it’s not just about making it through tough times. It’s about searching for reasons to keep moving forward, even when the odds feel stacked against you. For a child who’s faced abandonment, the road is long and often difficult. But along the way, there are moments of beauty, moments of connection, that make it all worthwhile. In the end, it’s those moments—however brief—that offer hope for a brighter future.
